notes: High-scale indexer for enterprise document archive (legal + engineering docs).
Goal: migrate in-house FAISS + custom reranker to a managed runtime to reduce ops and unit cost.
Target index size: 150M vectors initial, plan to grow to 750M within 12 months; goal 1B+ long-term.
Queries: mixed workload — 70% low-latency single-vector lookups (p95 < 40ms), 30% batch semantic reranking (hundreds to thousands of candidates per query).
Cost sensitivity: current infra ops cost ~ $1.3M/year for hosting and engineering time; target is 3-4x lower unit cost or equivalent with better SLAs.
Current stack: custom FAISS HNSW on NVMe-backed servers, embeddings produced by in-house model (retraining quarterly).
Model preferences: open 7B-13B encoder-only/dual-encoder for embeddings; reranker: 2-4B cross-encoder options (quantizable).

Technical constraints: must support cold-start indexing throughput >= 200K vectors/hr via bulk loader and streaming ingestion; nearline batch backfills; disk-backed shards with warm KV cache at runtime.
Operational needs: canary index rollouts, per-route cost dashboards, token-level tracing for reranker calls.
Security: on-prem appliance considered due to data residency and E2E kms requirement; audit logs retention 7 years for legal compliance.
Quote from CTO (Aug 2 call): "We need predictable unit economics at scale — not just raw throughput. If Redwood can show per-query $0.00X with fallback guarantees, we'll proceed."
Want Redwood Optimize to recommend batching/bucket strategies and quantization profile to hit latency/cost targets.
Feasibility POC approved by infra — scope: ingest 150M synthetic vectors, produce p95 query latency report for 1k QPS mixed workload, cost projection for 12 months.
